title: Grateful Dead Live at Alpine Valley Music Theatre on 1986-06-29
lineage: The Master Cassettes were played back with Azimuth adjustment on a Nakamichi CD1 into a Korg MR1000 at DSF 1 bit 5.6MHz. Subsequent conversion to 24/96 AIFF done via Korg Audiogate software. Redbook CDR standard 16/44.1 files were created using Bias Peak, Izotope Ozone's MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions)
source: 2 Nakamichi CM100s/ CP4>Sony WMD6 w/Teac MDX90 cassette masters. No Dolby was used on the Master Cassettes. Sec 2 Row KK Seat 44 Stand head height

ai_review.summary: Audience‑sourced tape captures an energetic Alpine ’86 show with solid opening numbers and a standout Sampson closer, but the recording is only fair in clarity.
ai_review.review: The performance is generally praised – the first three songs are described as “solid” and the second set feels “energetic, playful, and dexterous,” with the Sampson close highlighted as a high point. Recording quality is mixed: some listeners call it a “great sounding audience” tape while others note muddiness, boominess and lack of board‑level clarity, making it an okay but not superb source.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is consistently described as good/energetic, while recording quality ranges from great to mediocre; the weighted average yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners note decent audience ambience and occasional clarity (“great sounding audience”), but also describe the tape as boomy, not clear, and less crisp than a soundboard. Overall the mix is acceptable for casual listening.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Opening three numbers are praised as solid; the second set is highlighted for its energy and audience interaction, making the show feel lively despite no specific complaints about pacing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s playing is noted as strong and healthy – “does not sound like a guy who's gonna be in a coma soon.”
